task.title: Update the SAML certificate or OIDC secret
task.shortdesc: Disable the Red Hat identity provider integration before you change or update your internal SAML certificate or OIDC secret. These changes are sometimes referred to as rotations. After the rotation, update the Red Hat IdP integration with the new certificate or secret information and re-enable.

ul.li: Confirm you are logged in to the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console as the Organization Administrator.
Ensure you have configured and enabled the Red Hat identity provider integration.
Ensure you can access your internal IdP and rotate the SAML certificate or OIDC secret.

prereq.note: You must disable the Red Hat IdP integration before changing your internal SAML certificate or OIDC secret. Failure to do so results in all users, including Organization Administrators, being unable to authenticate. If this happens, contact Red Hat Customer Service.

step.cmd: Navigate to Settings > Authentication Policy > Identity Provider Integration. Your enabled integration is displayed.

info.note: While the identity provider is disabled, users will be able to log in with their Red Hat credentials.

The service provider metadata URL will become unavailable while the identity provider is disabled. You can still download the metadata information in .xml format from the configuration page by clicking the Download service provider metadata button.

step.cmd: Generate and update the SAML certificate or OIDC secret in your organization’s identity provider.
Update the Red Hat IdP integration SAML certificate or OIDC secret.
When finished, click Test and enable. The testing step is required after any update to your IdP integration.
On a successful test, click Enable to re-enable for your organization.
